description: PaymentMethod is a base class with a process method. Implement CreditCardPayment and PayPalPayment so they inherit from PaymentMethod and override process: CreditCardPayment must return "Processed via credit card" and PayPalPayment must return "Processed via PayPal". The base PaymentMethod.process can return any placeholder.
test_code:
import pytest
from main import PaymentMethod, CreditCardPayment, PayPalPayment

test_cases = [
    (CreditCardPayment, "Processed via credit card"),
    (PayPalPayment, "Processed via PayPal"),
]

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("payment_class", "expected_output"), test_cases
)
def test_process(payment_class, expected_output):
    print("\n---------------------------------")
    print(f"Inputs: {payment_class.__name__}")
    result = payment_class().process()
    print(f"Expected: {expected_output}")
    print(f"Actual:   {result}")
    assert result == expected_output


@pytest.mark.validate
def test_payments_process_polymorphically():
    payments: list[PaymentMethod] = [CreditCardPayment(), PayPalPayment()]
    print("\n---------------------------------")
    print(f"Inputs: {[type(p).__name__ for p in payments]}")
    results = [payment.process() for payment in payments]
    print(f"Expected: ['Processed via credit card', 'Processed via PayPal']")
    print(f"Actual:   {results}")
    assert results == ["Processed via credit card", "Processed via PayPal"]


@pytest.mark.validate
def test_payments_are_payment_methods():
    print("\n---------------------------------")
    print(f"Inputs: CreditCardPayment(), PayPalPayment()")
    print(f"Expected: both instances of PaymentMethod")
    print(f"Actual:   {isinstance(CreditCardPayment(), PaymentMethod)}, {isinstance(PayPalPayment(), PaymentMethod)}")
    assert isinstance(CreditCardPayment(), PaymentMethod)
    assert isinstance(PayPalPayment(), PaymentMethod)
